claims.explanation: Thiocolchicoside is a colchicine-site tubulin binder whose anticancer activity is linked to microtubule destabilization and NF-κB pathway inhibition, so selectivity likely reflects dependence on microtubule dynamics and NF-κB-driven survival signaling rather than GABA receptor expression. TP53 pathway inactivation and high NF-κB/anti-apoptotic tone (e.g., Bcl-2 family, XIAP) would sensitize cells, while intact p53 and low proliferative/microtubule dependency would protect.

features.basis: Damaging TP53 mutations dominate the most-killed lines, consistent with loss of p53-mediated apoptosis restraint after microtubule/NF-κB stress
Thiocolchicoside downregulates NF-κB and its regulated survival genes, so high NF-κB activity predicts greater dependence
Bcl-2 is an NF-κB-regulated survival factor suppressed by thiocolchicoside; high expression would blunt apoptosis
XIAP is an NF-κB-regulated inhibitor of apoptosis downregulated by thiocolchicoside
Thiocolchicoside increases Bax and decreases Bcl-2, shifting cells toward apoptosis
Thiocolchicoside binds tubulin and forms membrane pores; high tubulin dependence favors sensitivity
KRAS-mutant lines (pancreas, lung) appear among sensitive lines, consistent with NF-κB-dependent survival
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines appear in the sensitive set, possibly via MAPK/NF-κB crosstalk
PTEN loss activates PI3K/NF-κB survival signaling, potentially increasing dependence on NF-κB
RB1 loss and cell-cycle dysregulation appear enriched in sensitive lines
CDKN2A loss is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is a weak/ambiguous predictor
Annotated GABA-A receptor target; expression could mediate non-cytotoxic signaling and reduce sensitivity
